newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: AKZO LAUNCHES FERTILITY DRUG PUREGON IN NETHS.
newsitem.headline: AKZO LAUNCHES FERTILITY DRUG PUREGON IN NETHS.

text.p: Chemical group Akzo Nobel NV said on Thursday its new fertility drug Puregon would be available to Dutch women undergoing in vitro fertilisation (IVF) or ovulation induction treatment with immediate effect.
"Our studies reveal that the use of Puregon increases the chances of a pregnancy through IVF from one in five to one in four," said Thijs Boerma, general director of Akzo unit Organon.
Puregon has several advantages compared to traditional fertility drugs, Organon said.
The duration of the treatment is shorter and the quantities to be used smaller, it said.
"Organon can now adequately respond to clients' increased demand for fertility drugs," Boerma said.
Last November, Akzo said it had high hopes for Puregon.
"In time, this (Puregon) could be a hundreds of millions of guilders market," Akzo's finance director Syb Bergsma said.
